overview: Host Laura Duggan and her husband Stephen Duggan present a travelogue of their journey down the Mississippi River, highlighting historical landmarks, plantations, and local culture. Medford Community Media station manager Kevin Harrington and crew member Jim also join the show to share their own travel experiences in New Orleans.

items.title: Introduction and Mississippi River Cruise
items.summary: Host Laura Duggan introduces the travelogue and guest Stephen Duggan to discuss the design, features, and navigation of the Viking river boat they took down the Mississippi River.

items.title: Greenville, Mississippi Stop
items.summary: The Duggans detail their stop in Greenville, Mississippi, where they experienced local blues, rock and roll, and traditional Southern food.

items.title: Vicksburg, Mississippi Stop
items.summary: The couple discusses the Civil War history of Vicksburg, showcasing state monument statues, historical artifacts, and the recovered ironclad USS Cairo.

items.title: Natchez, Mississippi Stop
items.summary: The Duggans describe visiting Natchez, Mississippi, including an historic bar once frequented by Mark Twain and the unfinished octagonal Longwood Estate.

items.title: Oakley Plantation and Slave Quarters
items.summary: The couple describes their stop at Oakley Plantation, highlighting historical slave quarters, skilled labor history, and artist John James Audubon's time tutoring there.

items.title: Cajun Swamp Tour
items.summary: The Duggans share stories and photos from a Cajun swamp boat ride where they encountered wild alligators and visited the grave of voodoo queen Julia Brown.

items.title: New Orleans and the French Quarter
items.summary: The couple recounts their time in New Orleans, showing footage of local architecture, a historic hotel's carousel bar, and street musicians playing during a jazz festival.

items.title: Station Crew Experiences
items.summary: Medford Community Media station manager Kevin Harrington and crew member Jim join the set to share their personal stories of traveling to New Orleans.

subject: Mississippi River Travelogue
